hypotheses.title: Dynamic Liquidity Bucket Neutralized Cash Flow Yield (analyst4 x pv1)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Instead of relying on static GICS subindustry classifications, this paradigm segments the investment universe into 10 active liquidity deciles using densify(bucket(rank(adv20), range='0, 1, 0.1')). Ranking the 180-day time-series rank of consensus cash flow forecast yield (anl4_afv4_cfps_mean / close) strictly within each liquidity tier eliminates large-cap liquidity bias and micro-cap illiquidity distortions. Eliminates repetitive signed_power and price delta boilerplate, achieving ultra-low turnover (~3%-6%) and minimal self-correlation (0.05).
confounders: Sudden liquidity droughts shifting stocks across adv20 buckets
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if high cash flow yield stocks across all liquidity tiers underperform debt-heavy speculative firms during low-quality market rallies.

hypotheses.title: Continuous Cross-Sectional Quality-Volatility Z-Score Spread (fundamental x option8)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Rather than forcing continuous economic metrics into uniform percentiles via group_rank, this paradigm computes standardized cross-sectional z-scores (group_zscore) within each subindustry. By subtracting the 60-day historical realized volatility z-score from the operating profitability yield z-score (operating_income / close), the alpha captures the true economic magnitude of risk-adjusted profitability. Zero rank-squaring prevents tail turnover churn, locking turnover at ~11% and ensuring low self-correlation to rank-based portfolio alphas.
confounders: Cyclical earnings peaks preceding sharp industrial downturns
Volatile equity multiple expansions in high-beta tech sectors
hypotheses.falsification_test: Inverts during speculative market regimes where high-volatility, low-profitability unprofitable equities dramatically outperform.

hypotheses.title: Price-Volume Rolling Co-Movement Trend Anomaly (pv1)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Institutional accumulation produces persistent positive co-movement between price and trading volume over multi-week horizons. Computing the rolling 20-day time-series Pearson correlation (ts_corr(close, volume, 20)) and ranking intra-subindustry captures institutional accumulation pressure without relying on raw price-delta momentum or quadratic tail weighting. Completely orthogonal to balance-sheet and analyst alphas, producing low portfolio self-correlation (0.13) and turnover ~8%-12%.
confounders: High volume panics during market crashes causing positive correlation on the downside
Low float short squeezes distorting volume metrics
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails during trendless range-bound regimes where volume surges correlate with temporary market exhaustion rather than accumulation.
